angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 486,990 km at 162.52 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.1531 +/- 0.0095 mas (same row, RUWE 0.94): 162.52 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.7 +/- 0.05 solar radii from Frensch et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2969 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...700A.118F/abstract): 486,990 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.71 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Frensch et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2969 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...700A.118F/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4738 +/- 100 K from Frensch et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2969 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...700A.118F/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Frensch et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2969 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...700A.118F/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2969.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.599, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
